item.text: {"search_note":"I found no 2024 evidence that Kishida created a dedicated civilian-oversight body for police, military, intelligence, or prisons, or a national human rights institution. The affirmative evidence is mostly indirect and strongest in political-finance reform and victim redress, while the negative evidence is structural persistence of abusive criminal-justice practices.","evidence":[{"title":"Policy Speech by Prime Minister Kishida to the 213th Session of the Diet","publisher":"Prime Minister’s Office of Japan","date":"January 30, 2024","url":"https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202401/30shiseihoshin.html","summary":"Kishida said he launched the Political Reform Headquarters, promised transparency and legal reforms, and framed 2024 as a year for compliance, accountability, and restoring trust in politics. This is indirect but real evidence of building anti-corruption oversight and reform machinery.","question_ids":["3B.4","3B.2"]},{"title":"Press Conference by Prime Minister Kishida","publisher":"Prime Minister’s Office of Japan","date":"June 21, 2024","url":"https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202406/21kaiken.html","summary":"Kishida said the government had amended the Political Funds Control Act and that the remaining work included boosting transparency, establishing a third-party body for inspections and audits, and continuing political reform. This is the clearest evidence of creating independent inspection capacity and complaint-handling-like oversight in 2024, albeit in political finance rather than abuse by security services.","question_ids":["3B.4","3B.2"]},{"title":"Meeting with Groups of Plaintiffs and Others in Lawsuits for State Redress over the Former Eugenic Protection Act","publisher":"Prime Minister’s Office of Japan","date":"July 17, 2024","url":"https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/actions/202407/17menkai.html","summary":"Kishida met plaintiffs in the forced-sterilization cases and personally offered apology and redress, which is direct state accountability and complaint resolution for a major past rights abuse.","question_ids":["3B.4","3B.1","3B.2"]},{"title":"Video Message by Prime Minister Kishida at the Symposium on Inclusive Society and Human Rights","publisher":"Prime Minister’s Office of Japan","date":"February 5, 2024","url":"https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202402/05_message.html","summary":"Kishida said unfair discrimination against foreigners, people with disabilities, Ainu people, and sexual minorities is unacceptable and tied government policy to rule of law and human dignity. This supports a pro-oversight, pro-rights posture, though it is not itself a concrete oversight mechanism.","question_ids":["3B.4","3B.3","3B.1"]},{"title":"World Report 2024: Japan","publisher":"Human Rights Watch","date":"2024","url":"https://www.hrw.org/world-report/2024/country-chapters/japan","summary":"HRW said Japan still lacked a national human rights institution and that its criminal-justice system remained abusive, including coercive questioning, repeated arrests, denial of bail, and weak legal access. This is the strongest negative evidence that Kishida did not build a robust independent abuse-oversight system.","question_ids":["3B.4","3B.1","3B.2"]},{"title":"Japan’s Abusive ‘Hostage Justice’ System Persists","publisher":"Human Rights Watch","date":"October 1, 2024","url":"https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/10/01/japans-abusive-hostage-justice-system-persists","summary":"HRW said abusive pretrial detention and coerced confessions were still ongoing, using the Hakamada case to show that independent correction of wrongful punishment remained inadequate. This undercuts any claim that Kishida had built strong due-process or abuse-review systems.","question_ids":["3B.4","3B.1","3B.2"]},{"title":"Japanese man acquitted of 1966 murders after 45 years on death row","publisher":"Reuters","date":"September 26, 2024","url":"https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/japanese-man-acquitted-of-1966-murders-after-45-years-on-death-row-3633320","summary":"Hakamada’s acquittal after 45 years on death row is evidence that the justice system still produced severe wrongful-punishment outcomes during Kishida’s term, suggesting weak independent correction mechanisms.","question_ids":["3B.4","3B.1","3B.2"]}]}
